To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel multifunctional compound has a high electron-transporting capability, a high hole-transporting capability and a high luminescence efficiency, which makes it possible to fabricate an electroluminescence device with a high efficiency.

a new multifunctional compound, 2-(4-n-butylphenyl)-5-(2-hydroxy-4-n-butyl)pyridin-6-yl)-1,3-bis(2,6-dimethylphenyl)benzene (BHBP), which integrates the hole-transport (HT), electrontransport (ET), and electroluminescence (EL) components into one molecule, was synthesized.

a new multifunctional boron-containing material, in which the hole transporting, electron transporting and emitting components are integrated into one single molecule, was synthesized and used to fabricate an electroluminescence device that exhibited a maximum luminance of 12,400 cd/m ^{2}, a maximum current efficiency of 1.9 cd/A, and a maximum power efficiency of 0.8 lm/W at 8 V.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of a new class of multifunctional compounds, in which the hole and electron transport, and emitting functions are integrated into a molecule, and their application in the fabrication of efficient single-layer light-emitting devices (LEDs).

the design, synthesis, and characterization of a new bipolar emitting boron bis(diphenylamino)pyridine compound, 1,6-di-(4-butylphenyl)-2-(4-diphenylammoniumphenyl)-4,5-dibromopyridine (BPPBPP), and its application in single-layer organic electroluminescence.

the design of a novel multifunctional molecule that can serve as an HT, ET, and EM material in an electroluminescence device, and the synthesis, characterization, and device performance of a single-layer device based on this molecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the device based on the new material is an efficient single-layer EL device with a high EL quantum efficiency (ηEL=0.8%), high luminance (I=1.5 cd cm−2 at 10 V), and low turn-on voltage (Von=2 V).
the device with the new material exhibits a maximum current efficiency of 3.2 cd/A, a power efficiency of 0.7 lm/W, and an EQE of 1.1% at the driving voltage of 8.0 V.
the present study demonstrates that a single-layer device can be fabricated with high efficiency by using the multifunctional compound as an emitting material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel single-layer electroluimincent device with a single molecular material that can be used as the HT, ET and EL component.

the single-layer electroluminiscence device based on this novel material has the following characteristics: (1) a low operating voltage, (2) a high luminous efficiency of 0.5 cd/A and (3) an excellent stability.
we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using a single molecule as an emitting, hole-transporting, and electron-transporting material for single-layer electroluminiscence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the device has an excellent electroluminescence (EL) efficiency of 4.5 cd A(-1), which is much better than those of the devices fabricated with the conventional single-layer emitting materials.

a single molecular material with the ability to transport both electrons and holes, and to emit light can serve as a multifunctional emitter for the fabrication of an efficient single-layer organic light emitting diode.
the incorporation of a boron atom into the pyridine ring of the 1,6-diarylpyridine molecule is effective for improving the electroluminescence properties of the device.
